title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone2: reproducibility packages for controlled-rail brachistochrones in conformal Kerr, Vaidya and McVittie spacetimes
description:
NonStationaryBrachistochrone2 contains the reproducibility packages for the second group of papers on controlled-rail brachistochrones: the fastest timelike worldline from a fixed departure event to a fixed spatial target, with free arrival time, when a controlled thrust holds the traveller at a maintained energy. The first group (Paper I, FLRW and Vaidya; Paper II, conformal Kerr) is archived as NonStationaryBrachistochrone.

The folder paper3 supports Paper III, Global minimality of controlled-rail brachistochrones in conformal Kerr and Vaidya spacetimes, and its supplementary material. The paper reads the rail as the null cone of an auxiliary metric and reduces the statements about specific transcendental quantities to finitely many explicit inequalities. The package contains:

  • 33 portable Bernstein curvature certificates for the Kerr equator, with an independent verifier that needs only the Python standard library, tampering tests, and generators that rebuild the certificates identically;
  • interval-arithmetic programs (unimodality on a grid of 20 cases, critical separations, the Maxwell angle) and outward-rounded Riemann sums;
  • 40 Wolfram Language scripts that check the symbolic derivations, with a launcher that accepts each log only against its expected outcome;
  • independent second implementations, including a Wolfram Language recheck of certificate leaves;
  • floating-point diagnostics, which illustrate and are not used as proofs;
  • the LaTeX sources of the paper and of the supplement, and the figure generators.

Every computer-assisted step of the paper is listed in paper3/RESULTS_MAP.md, in the order of the text, with the script that checks it, the log of our run and the kind of check (exact, certificate, interval arithmetic, numerical). The script paper3/run_all.sh runs everything and applies acceptance checks to the recorded logs; the archived full run on commit e614e87 (Python 3.13.2, Mathematica 13.3.1) passed all 30 jobs. The folder paper4, for controlled-rail brachistochrones in the McVittie metric, is in preparation.
